rationale: The crafted witness shows a follower's decided index can decrease; this run measures the same property under a random lossy schedule. The existing five-node stress now tracks each node's maximum decided index across actions and counts decreases, emitting the first regression. The declared predicate is decided monotonicity (no node reports fewer decided entries than it previously reported), gated on progressed so a decision-free run cannot satisfy it. A violation would be naturalistic evidence for the recorded decided-regression defect; zero would bound its incidence under these exercised conditions.

scope.description: Five-node, 900-action randomized stress with seed 0x452821e638d01377, run id 9 and 20 percent message loss, tracking each node's maximum decided index across actions and counting any decrease, in addition to the pairwise agreement check and fair-delivery convergence.
assumptions: Messages may be delivered out of order or dropped; ticks drive elections and resends.
A decided index decrease is defined against that node's own earlier observed decided index within the same run.
No snapshots, trimming or reconfiguration are used.
excluded: Snapshots, compaction, flexible quorums, reconfiguration, crash-restart and Byzantine participants.

experiment.prefix: Same stress construction as the agreement runs, with seed 0x452821e638d01377 and run id 9. After each action and the prefix comparison, read each node's get_decided_idx and compare with its recorded maximum: a lower value increments regressions and records first_regression. After the loop, run the fair-delivery convergence phase, recompute progressed, and emit the safety event with appended, delivered, dropped, divergences, first_divergence, progressed, regressions, first_regression and decided indices.

comparisons.description: Monotonic decided index: with progressed true, no node may report a decided index lower than one it already reported.
